C1799.title: Creating “Gossip Groups” to Spread Rumors Convicted as Crime of Picking Quarrels and Provoking Trouble

crime of picking quarrels and provoking trouble
C1799.summary: The Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai found that defendants Xiao Wang and Xiao Li, knowing the information was fabricated, still disseminated it widely online, causing serious disruption to public order, constituting the crime of picking quarrels and provoking trouble. They were sentenced to nine months and seven months in prison respectively, with criminal tools confiscated. The case involves using online groups to spread rumors; the defendants did not appeal after sentencing.
C1799.description:
This case was tried by the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai. The defendants Xiao Wang and Xiao Li established so-called “gossip groups” and other online groups, and despite knowing the information was fabricated, they still disseminated false content widely online. This behavior triggered massive attention and reposting by netizens, seriously disrupting both cyberspace order and real-world public order.

The court determined after trial that the two defendants' actions constituted the crime of picking quarrels and provoking trouble. Ultimately, Xiao Wang was sentenced to nine months in prison, and Xiao Li was sentenced to seven months in prison, with their criminal tools confiscated according to law. After the judgment was pronounced, neither defendant filed an appeal, and the judgment has taken effect.

This case is a typical criminal case involving the use of online groups to spread rumors, reflecting that even after refutation, those who do not cease but continue to maliciously disseminate false information will face severe criminal penalties. The case carries significant warning implications for online content compliance and the governance of false information.
